19	# CSR transport bring-up for a new Andes core
20	
21	Inputs you need from the user (ask if missing):
22	- The AndeStar V5 SPA PDF for the core family (the repo carries
23	  `AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` for the current cores).
24	- The engine name (e.g. `ax45mpv_premium`) and a built vsim checkout
25	  (`VSIM_BIN_DIR` in `config.env` points at its `build/`).
26	- Optionally the matching QEMU `-cpu` name for the oracle leg.
27	
28	The goal: every CSR the core implements and the ROI can touch is restored at
29	resume, re-read at drain, and `--verify`-compared -- and every CSR the core
30	does NOT implement is gated off, because the batched Program-Buffer sweep
31	faults (cmderr=3) on a single over-claimed CSR.
32	
33	Work in this order. Each phase has a reference file with the details --
34	read it when you reach the phase, not before.
35	
36	## Phase 0: establish ground truth
37	
38	The engine's compiled-in config is the ONLY truth about what it implements.
39	Read `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` (the BUILD directory copy --
40	the `external/` source tree can differ from what was actually built) and
41	`sim_<engine> --describe`. Do not trust QEMU: its gdbstub exposes CSRs the
42	vsim RTL does not implement (QEMU models a fuller core), and restoring or
43	sweeping one of those stalls or faults the Debug Module.
44	
45	## Phase 1: mine the spec
46	
47	Run `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf>` to refresh
48	`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (needs PyMuPDF; use a venv). Then pull,
49	for each CSR the core claims: the IM Requirement (existence condition), the
50	Access Mode, and the reset value. The SPA has a fixed per-CSR layout and a
51	consolidated existence table (Table 13) -- see
52	`references/spec-mining.md` for the exact headers and extraction recipes.
53	
54	## Phase 2: classify dispositions
55	
56	Run `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` and
57	the guard `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py`. The guard enforces
58	inventory == matrix == ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`), so a CSR added to
59	the wire format without a disposition (or vice versa) fails loudly. New
60	transported CSRs are one X-macro line in `state_abi.h`
61	(`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` / `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`); every consumer
62	(plugin drain, restore, drain re-read, verify) iterates the same list.
63	
64	## Phase 3: bind capability gates
65	
66	For each transported CSR, map its IM Requirement to a gate in the vsim
67	repo's `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (address -> gate) and bind the gate to a
68	`_NDS_*` config macro in `andes_caps_config.hpp` (absent macro reads as
69	"off" -- never a compile error). The gate must encode the SPEC's existence
70	condition, not a plausibly-related feature; two real bugs came from getting
71	this wrong. Follow TDD: model the new engine's config shape as a caps
72	helper in `tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp` and write the failing
73	expectation first. Read `references/caps-gating.md` -- it carries the
74	hard-won rules and the write-prerequisite (setup ordering) requirements.
75	
76	## Phase 4: reset values and verify exclusions
77	
78	Two reset-value sources exist and they legitimately differ:
79	- The SPA reset table (documentation; many fields are IM = implementation
80	  determined or DC = don't care).
81	- The EMPIRICAL baseline the simulator drains from the freshly reset hart
82	  (cached per engine build + ELF). The liveness gate compares against this
83	  one -- it is self-truthing, so spec IM/DC values need no manual table.
84	
85	Where QEMU's reset differs from the engine's reset for a CSR the program
86	never writes (e.g. `msp_bound`, `milmb` enable bit), a strict compare
87	false-positives: add it to `andes_verify_excluded` in
88	`driver/state_diff.cpp` with a comment naming the divergence. Do NOT
89	exclude a CSR to hide a transport bug -- exclusion is only for
90	engine-implementation artifacts.
91	
92	## Phase 5: validate (the ladder)
93	
94	Run bottom-up; each rung catches what the one below cannot. The key
95	insight: the tolerant abstract path MASKS capability bugs (a faulting read
96	mirrors as zero, QEMU drains zero too, --verify falsely matches), so only
97	the batched CSR sweep truly validates the caps table -- it faults on an
98	over-claim and bisects to NAME the offending CSR. A cold-cache hybrid run

100	failure playbook: `references/validation.md`.
101	
102	## Phase 6: register the engine (per-engine test completeness)
103	
104	andesim is a commercial product: every supported engine BUILD must ship its
105	own complete, machine-checked CSR test artifacts -- and a rebuild of the
106	same core with a different config counts as a NEW registration (the

1	# Mining the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF
2	
3	## Extract text once, grep many times
4	
5	```sh
6	python -m venv /tmp/pdfvenv && /tmp/pdfvenv/bin/pip -q install pymupdf
7	/tmp/pdfvenv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
8	import fitz, sys
9	doc = fitz.open("AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf")
10	with open("/tmp/spa.txt", "w") as f:
11	    for i, page in enumerate(doc, 1):
12	        f.write(f"===PAGE {i}===\n" + page.get_text())
13	EOF
14	```
15	
16	The repo already automates the inventory step:
17	`scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py <spec.pdf> [out.csv]` writes
18	`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (addr, privilege, name, mode, section).
19	Run it when the spec revision changes; the committed CSV is the checked-in
20	truth the coverage guard reads.
21	
22	## Per-CSR section layout (chapters 8-10)
23	
24	Every CSR gets a section with fixed headers -- grep for the mnemonic, then
25	read the block:
26	
27	```
28	8.3.8
29	User Scratch Register
30	Mnemonic Name: uscratch
31	IM Requirement: misa[13]==1 (N extension)     <- existence condition
32	Access Mode: User                              <- privilege mode
33	CSR Address: 0x040 (standard read/write)
34	XLEN: 64 and 32
35	<bit-field diagram: per-field name, type (RW/RO/W1C/...), reset value>
36	```
37	
38	- `IM Requirement:` is THE existence condition. This is what the caps gate
39	  must encode (Phase 3). "Always" means gate ALWAYS.
40	- `Access Mode:` gives the privilege mode the user asked about ("which mode
41	  supports this CSR"): Machine / Supervisor / User / Debug.
42	- Field types use the terminology page (chapter 9.1): IM = implementation
43	  determined, DC = reset value is don't care, RO/WO/RW/W1C/WS/RAZWI.
44	  IM and DC reset values CANNOT be tabled from the spec -- that is exactly
45	  why the empirical reset baseline (Phase 4) is the source the liveness
46	  gate uses.
47	
48	## Table 13: the consolidated existence table
49	
50	"Table 13: Existence configuration condition(s)" lists CSR groups against
51	their conditions in one place -- faster than walking every section, and the
52	authoritative cross-check when a per-section IM Requirement reads
53	ambiguously. Real rows:
54	
55	```
56	mcounterinten                 mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1
57	mcounterwen                   (mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[20]==1) // user
58	mcountermask_m
59	mcountermask_u
60	mcounterovf
61	mcountermask_s                (mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[18]==1) // supervisor
62	mcounteren                    misa[20]==1 // user mode
63	```
64

Mnemonic Name: uscratch

Access Mode: User                              <- privilege mode

  determined, DC = reset value is don't care, RO/WO/RW/W1C/WS/RAZWI.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Classify every spec CSR by its hybrid-handoff transport disposition.

The OFFLINE mirror of the wire-format transport set. It reads the spec inventory
snapshot (tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv, produced by extract_csr_inventory.py)
and assigns each CSR a disposition under the supported envelope: bare-metal,
single-hart, M-mode or M+U-mode, trap-free ROI.

The policy here must match what include/hybrid/state_abi.h actually transports.
The guard test (tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.*) cross-checks the
two, so a CSR added to the ABI without a matching disposition (or vice versa)
fails CI -- the "nothing missed" flywheel.

Dispositions (see docs/csr_coverage.ipynb for the full legend):
  TRANSPORT_NOW  already carried in hybrid_state_v1
  NEW            writable M-mode plain state -- expansion target
  NEW_TRIG       debug-trigger CSR (shares the Debug Module; transported guarded)
  NEW_UDELTA     U-mode Andes control; transported, exercised only in M+U
  CONST_RO       read-only config/info -- engine derives it; nothing to exchange
  EXCL_RV32      RV32 high-half shadow -- irrelevant on RV64
  EXCL_SIDEFX    read/write has side effects -- not architectural state
  EXCL_W1C_HW    write-1-clear, hardware-driven (like mip)
  EXCL_INDIRECT  miselect/mireg access mechanism, not a direct register
  EXCL_NEXT      U-mode N-extension trap state (trap-free ROI + usually absent)
  EXCL_DEBUG     Debug-mode CSR the handoff itself drives
  EXCL_MODE      S-mode / Hypervisor -- outside the M / M+U envelope
  EXCL_TRAP      detailed trap-cause latch, live only after a trap

Usage:
  classify_csr_coverage.py <csr_inventory.csv>            # write csr_coverage.csv beside it
  classify_csr_coverage.py <csr_inventory.csv> --stdout   # print, do not write
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# CSRs already carried in hybrid_state_v1 today (Bucket A). Names as the spec
# summary tables print them (range rows kept verbatim, e.g. pmpaddr1~63).
TRANSPORT_NOW = {
    "mstatus", "mepc", "mtvec", "mcause", "mtval", "mscratch", "medeleg",
    "mideleg", "mie", "mip", "mcycle", "minstret", "satp", "fcsr", "frm",
    "fﬂags",  # "fflags" with the fi-ligature the PDF emits
    "JVT", "mcache_ctl", "mmisc_ctl", "mxstatus", "mpft_ctl", "mclk_ctl",
    "milmb", "mdlmb", "mecc_code", "mhsp_ctl", "msp_bound", "msp_base",
    "mcountermask_m", "uitb", "ucode",
    "pmpcfg0", "pmpcfg1", "pmpcfg2", "pmpcfg3", "pmpcfg4~15",
    "pmpaddr0", "pmpaddr1~63",
    "pmacfg0", "pmacfg2", "pmaaddr0~47",
}

# Per-name decisions that override the structural defaults below.
OVERRIDE = {
    "misa": "CONST_RO", "tinfo": "CONST_RO", "tdata3": "CONST_RO",
    "mintstatus": "EXCL_RO",
    # side-effecting: reading or writing performs an action, so the value is not
    # state to round-trip.
    "mnxti": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "mscratchcsw": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
    "mscratchcswl": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "mcctlcommand": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
    "mintsel_jal": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "pushmcause": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
    "pushmepc": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "pushmxstatus": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
    "wfe": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "txevt": "EXCL_SIDEFX", "ucctlcommand": "EXCL_SIDEFX",
    "mcounterovf": "EXCL_W1C_HW",
    "miselect": "EXCL_INDIRECT", "mireg": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
    "mireg2": "EXCL_INDIRECT", "mireg3": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
    "mireg4": "EXCL_INDIRECT", "mireg5": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
    "mireg6": "EXCL_INDIRECT",
    "dcsr": "EXCL_DEBUG", "dpc": "EXCL_DEBUG", "dscratch0": "EXCL_DEBUG",
    "dscratch1": "EXCL_DEBUG", "scontext": "EXCL_MODE",

anyway: both built engines are M-only.

| Reset value | 0 ("The default value of this register is 0.") |
| Fields | CY(0), IR(2), HPM3..HPM6(3..6); bits 7..31 read as 0 |
| Alias | Table 14 "Summary of Aliased CSRs": `mcountermask_s, scountermask_s` -- one physical register, two addresses |
